chunks: And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Aban, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah has assigned to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) four thousand angels, disheveled and dusty, weeping for him from the rising of dawn until the sun declines. When the sun declines, four thousand angels descend and four thousand angels ascend, and they do not cease weeping for him until dawn rises, and he mentioned the hadith.

key_terms.شُعْثٌ غُبْرٌ: Disheveled and covered with dust (with dust), describing the state of the angels
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ (ع): The grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Who are the angels weeping at the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.) according to Kamil al-Ziyarat?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic significance of Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom, portraying the angels as perpetual mourners whose continuous weeping sanctifies his grave. The description of them as 'disheveled and dusty' (*shuuthun ghubrun*) emphasizes the raw, unadorned nature of their grief, reinforcing the Shia theological view that the Ahl al-Bayt’s suffering resonates throughout the heavens. This perpetual mourning serves as a spiritual model for believers, linking earthly remembrance with celestial devotion.
